title: A combined deep-learning and clinical model predicts positive BI-RADS 4A mammography lesions
summary: In a retrospective cohort of 590 women with BI-RADS 4A lesions and pathology results, a model combining age, nipple discharge, ultrasound BI-RADS assessment, and Mammomat AI classification had AUCs of 0.85 in training, 0.82 in internal validation, and 0.84 in an external hospital cohort of 123 patients. The selected population and retrospective design limit generalization; diagnostic performance does not establish reduced biopsies or improved clinical outcomes.
ai_technology: Mammomat AI v3 deep-learning image detection, segmentation and classification integrated with clinical predictors
organization: The Eighth Affiliated Hospital, Sun Yat-sen University

evidence.tested: The combined model was evaluated against pathology in retrospective training and internal cohorts and an external cohort from a second hospital; the reported AUCs were 0.85, 0.82, and 0.84, respectively.
evidence.unknown: The cohorts were retrospective and restricted to BI-RADS 4A patients; improved patient outcomes or reduced biopsy rates were not demonstrated.
evidence.ai_role: Mammomat AI v3 supplied mammographic classification results combined with clinical factors in the prediction model.

source_review.scope: Full primary publisher article, including Methods, Results, author affiliations and publication history
